The return window and refund timing are separate requirements. Do not treat a request as approved until it has been reviewed under this procedure. For cases involving spoiled perishable food, use the Fresh Grocery spoilage claim process rather than the standard return process.

excerpts.title: Host Scheduling and Shift Handover
excerpts.content:
SOP | All departments
Host Scheduling and Shift Handover > Steps

1. Live Operations publishes the schedule for the next week every Thursday.
2. Check your assigned shifts and raise scheduling issues with Live Operations.
3. Keep each host on camera for at most 4 hours a day.
4. Arrange a 15-minute overlap between two hosts at each handover.
5. Before the outgoing host leaves, update the handover sheet with stock status, promises made in the chat that are still open, and any complaints.
6. Review the handover sheet with the incoming host during the overlap.
7. For a shift swap, give 48 hours' notice and get confirmation from the Live Operations team before treating the swap as approved.
8. If a swap is not confirmed, follow the published schedule and contact Live Operations about coverage.
9. Flag missing handover information or unresolved issues to the incoming host and Live Operations.

excerpts.title: Refund and Return Requests
excerpts.content:
SOP | All departments
Refund and Return Requests > Procedure

1. Check the item and request. a. Confirm the delivery date and whether the item is within the 30-day return window. Customers can return an item within 30 days of delivery. b. Perishable food cannot be returned unless it arrived spoiled. For a spoiled item, follow the Fresh Grocery spoilage claim process. c. Record a reason code for every request. Use one of these codes: wrong item, damaged, changed mind or quality issue.
2. Review the request and determine the refund amount. a. For an item bought at a livestream-only price, calculate the refund using the price the customer paid, not the list price. b. If the refund is above $500, obtain sign-off from a Customer Service team lead before issuing it.
3. Process the return and refund. a. Provide the customer with the applicable return instructions and track the returned item. b. Issue the refund within 5 business days after the returned item is received. c. Record the outcome and any required approval in the order record.
4. Direct livestream questions to the order page. a. Hosts and moderators must never promise a refund in the live chat. b. Hosts and moderators must point the customer to the order page to submit or follow up on a request.

Refund and Return Requests > Definitions

Return window — The period in which a customer may return an eligible item, measured from delivery.

Reason code — The required classification recorded for each refund or return request.

Livestream-only price — A price available only for an item bought during a livestream.

Fresh Grocery spoilage claim process — The process for claims involving perishable food that arrived spoiled.

ROI (the formula changed; here is why)
excerpts.content:
Post-campaign review | Beauty | Beauty Black Friday Live | 2025-11-18 | Host: Tommy Walter
Beauty Black Friday Live - Post-Campaign Review > ROI (the formula changed; here is why)

The first two versions were wrong. The first one subtracted only the operating cost, not the product cost, so ROI looked too high. The second one added the product cost to the denominator, which is also wrong: product cost is already deducted in campaign_products.profit (profit = sales - product cost; the customer pays for the goods, it is not money the company spent on this campaign). The real question is: how much profit did the marketing spend (the operating cost) bring in?

- Total product profit (sum of profit over the 3 featured products in campaign_products, product cost already deducted): $168.8K
- Actual operating cost (campaigns.actual_operating_cost): $73.6K
- ROI = total product profit / operating cost = 168.8 / 73.6 ≈ 2.29: every $1 of marketing spend brought back about $2.29 of product profit

Both numbers now come from structured fields (SUM(campaign_products.profit) and campaigns.actual_operating_cost), so the review no longer estimates them by hand or improvises a formula.

Findings:

1. Serum had the highest margin (58.26%), the most units and the most profit. The plan positioned it as the traffic driver; it turned out to be the most profitable product as well. A winter skincare staple does not need a deep discount to sell.
2. Sheet masks had the highest sales but the lowest margin (34.52%). The "20% off two boxes" bundle drove volume and gave away most of the margin.
3. Lipstick and serum came back at almost twice the return rate of sheet masks (about 19% vs 10%). For lipstick this is probably shade mismatch; worth checking the return reasons before the next campaign.
4. Operating cost was 3.5% over budget, the overrun the plan warned about ("ad placement bids usually rise during Black Friday"). It was small this time, but it points the same way as other seasonal campaigns.

excerpts.title: Livestream Incident Response
excerpts.content:
SOP | All departments
Livestream Incident Response > Procedure

1. Respond to a dropped stream. a. The producer switches to the backup stream within 2 minutes of the stream dropping. b. While the producer switches streams, the host keeps talking and gives viewers a brief update.
2. Respond to a wrong price on screen. a. Remove the product link at once. b. Review orders placed at the wrong price. Honor orders if the error is less than 30% off the right price. Otherwise, cancel the orders and provide an apology coupon of $10. c. The host should give a brief, accurate update and avoid confirming an order outcome before it is reviewed.
3. Respond to a product that sells out mid-stream. a. The host announces that the product has sold out and moves to the next product. b. Do not promise a waitlist on air.
4. Respond to a raid of offensive comments. a. The moderator turns on slow mode and blocks the accounts posting offensive comments. b. The host does not respond to the comments and continues the stream.
5. Document and follow up. a. The responsible Live Operations staff member files the incident log within 1 hour after the stream ends. b. Send a short post-incident note the next day. Include a concise summary of what happened and the actions taken.

SOP | Consumer Electronics
Product Demo Setup for Livestreams (Consumer Electronics) > Procedure

1. Select and prepare demo units. a. Confirm the product matches the livestream plan and is in working condition. b. Ensure all demo units are fully charged and running the latest firmware before the stream. c. Set up a backup unit for every product that is demonstrated. Confirm it is charged, functional, and ready to use.
2. Prepare the demonstration area. a. Place each product and its accessories within the host’s reach. b. Keep cables and other equipment organized so they do not obstruct the host or appear as a safety hazard. c. Confirm products are clean and positioned so viewers can see relevant features.
3. Test connectivity and presentation. a. Test screen mirroring 30 minutes before the stream. Confirm the correct device is connected and its display is visible in the stream. b. Check that any required connections, controls, and demonstration content work as intended. c. If screen mirroring or another essential function fails, troubleshoot before the stream. Use the backup unit when appropriate and notify the production lead if the issue remains unresolved.
4. Conduct product demonstrations. a. Demonstrate product features accurately and follow the livestream plan. b. Hosts never compare the product with a competitor’s by name. Keep comparisons focused on the product’s own features and intended use. c. Demonstrate earbuds and speakers below 85 dB. Monitor the sound level during the demonstration and lower it if it reaches the limit. d. Do not continue a demonstration if the product becomes unsafe, stops working, or cannot be presented accurately. Switch to the backup unit or inform the production lead.
5. Complete the setup check. a. Confirm the demo unit and backup unit are ready and accessible. b. Confirm the host understands the demonstration plan and the requirements in this procedure. c. Report unresolved equipment or setup issues to the production lead before the stream begins.

excerpts.title: Customer Complaint Escalation
excerpts.content:
SOP | All departments
Customer Complaint Escalation > Procedure

1. Log every complaint. a. Record each complaint in the CRM and include its complaint ID. b. Add the customer’s concern, relevant communications and actions taken. Keep the record factual and update it as the complaint progresses.
2. Handle Level 1 complaints. a. A support agent must answer the complaint within 4 hours. b. The agent should acknowledge the concern, clarify any information needed, and explain the next action. The agent remains responsible for the complaint unless it meets a higher escalation level.
3. Escalate to Level 2 when required. a. A team lead takes over if the complaint is unresolved after 24 hours. b. A team lead also takes over if the customer threatens a public review, whether or not 24 hours have passed. c. The team lead reviews the CRM record, coordinates the response, and keeps the customer informed until the complaint is resolved or escalated again.
4. Escalate to Level 3 when required. a. Trust & Safety and Legal take over for any complaint involving an injury, a product safety issue or a regulator’s inquiry. b. Notify both teams promptly and provide the CRM record and relevant supporting information. Do not make commitments or speculate about responsibility while those teams review the matter. c. Continue to preserve related communications and follow the direction of Trust & Safety and Legal.
5. Keep compensation private. a. Compensation is never discussed in public comments. Discuss it only in a private message. b. If a customer raises compensation in a public comment, acknowledge the concern without discussing compensation and invite the customer to continue by private message.

The Home New Product Launch ran from Jan 8, 2026 to Feb 16, 2026, with Lisa Hernandez hosting across 40 streamed days. The campaign finished with strong sales and conversion, and the live audience stayed within the target range at peak. The results suggest the product demonstrations gave viewers enough reason to move from watching to buying. excerpts.title: Sale Event Inventory Check (Beauty)
excerpts.content:
SOP | Beauty
Sale Event Inventory Check (Beauty) > When to Use

Use this procedure before every Beauty sale stream. The check is done 72 hours before the stream so the team has time to resolve stock, shelf-life, shade availability, and storage issues before products are presented to customers. Beauty inventory needs a product-level review: a total count can look adequate while specific lipstick or foundation shades are short, expired stock can be mixed with eligible stock, and testers or free samples can make sellable quantities appear higher than they are. The review also confirms that temperature-sensitive serums are stored correctly. These checks protect customers from products with too little shelf life, prevent unavailable shades from being offered, and give the stream team a reliable view of what it can sell. The Beauty category manager signs off the check after the required reviews are complete.
